summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Sertoli cells form the Blood-Testis Barrier (BTB) via occluding tight junctions, isolating haploid germ cells from autoimmune destruction. Spermiogenesis cytological metamorphosis: Golgi -> Acrosome cap, Centrioles -> Tail, Mitochondria -> spiral Nebenkern middle piece, sheds excess cytoplasm. Accessory glands: Seminal vesicles (60% alkaline, Fructose/Prostaglandins), Prostate (30% citrate/PSA), Bulbourethral/Cowper's (alkaline lubricating mucus).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SPERMIOGENESIS METAMORPHOSIS
                        
   Spherical Spermatid ($n$) ──► Golgi Apparatus forms **Acrosome** (Cap)
                             ──► Centrioles form Axial Filament / Tail
                             ──► Mitochondria aggregate into spiral **Nebenkern** (Middle Piece)
                             ──► Sheds excess cytoplasm ──► **Spermatozoon**
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 2.1 Sertoli Cells & The Blood-Testis Barrier (BTB)

```
                      SEMINIFEROUS TUBULE CROSS-SECTION
                      
   Basal Lamina ──► Spermatogonia ($2n$) ──► Primary Spermatocyte ($2n$)
                                                    │
   Sertoli Cell Tight Junction (BTB) ───────────────┼─────────────────
                                                    ▼
   Lumen ◄── Spermatozoa ($n$) ◄── Spermatid ($n$) ◄── Secondary Spermatocyte ($n$)
```

- **Blood-Testis Barrier (BTB)**: Adjacent Sertoli cells form occluding tight junctions near the basal lamina, dividing the seminiferous epithelium into a basal compartment (containing spermatogonia) and an adluminal compartment (containing meiotic cells and spermatids). This isolates haploid germ cells ($n$) expressing novel surface auto-antigens from autoimmune destruction by circulating antibodies and lymphocytes.
- **Sertoli Secretory Products**:
  1. **Androgen-Binding Protein (ABP)**: Concentrates testosterone within the seminiferous tubule lumen under FSH stimulation.
  2. **Inhibin**: Peptide hormone that selectively exerts negative feedback on the anterior pituitary to suppress FSH secretion.
  3. **Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH)**: Induces regression of Müllerian ducts in male fetuses.

### 2.2 Spermiogenesis & Spermiation
- **Spermiation**: The detachment and release of mature spermatozoa from Sertoli nurse cells into the seminiferous tubule lumen.

### 2.3 Male Accessory Glands
1. **Seminal Vesicles (Paired, $\approx 60\%$)**: Alkaline fluid with **Fructose** and **Prostaglandins**.
2. **Prostate Gland (Single, $\approx 30\%$)**: Slightly acidic fluid with **Citrate** and **PSA**.
3. **Bulbourethral (Cowper's) Glands (Paired)**: Alkaline lubricating mucus.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Nebenkern Mitochondrial Sheath
conceptBreakdown.title: Nebenkern Mitochondrial Sheath
conceptBreakdown.content: During spermiogenesis, mitochondria fuse and wrap spirally around the axoneme in the sperm middle piece (forming the Nebenkern), generating high-density ATP to fuel the dynein ATPase arms of the flagellar axoneme.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Semen Volume & Sperm Count
conceptBreakdown.title: Semen Volume & Sperm Count
conceptBreakdown.content: Normal human ejaculate is 2-5 mL containing 200-300 million sperm. For normal fertility, at least 60% must possess normal shape and size, and at least 40% must show vigorous forward motility.
